set.layering_notes: Reclassified from other to loan in the November 8, 2026 audit: the Affordable Housing Special Revenue Fund is deployable at Board discretion and its only recent use was forgivable loans (up to $73,318 per household) under the Caldor Fire Grizzly Flats Homeowner Rebuild Program (Resolution 064-2026, April 7, 2026). Do not underwrite County gap money in El Dorado. The county has no inclusionary fee revenue yet, no housing bond and no sales tax measure, so the Trust Fund is capitalized only by occasional conduit issuance fees and permit-related deposits. The planned Affordable Housing Ordinance (inclusionary with an in-lieu fee set by a fee nexus study now being procured) is intended to expand the Trust Fund, which is the only path to a real county gap source in the next few years. County housing staff capacity is thin: a single Administrative Analyst position was reinstated in April 2026 and HousingINC runs the program in the interim, so allow time for any County action (Board Policy A-6 resolutions, TIF offsets, TEFRA hearings).
set.audit_note: Board item 26-0542 confirms the Special Revenue Fund balance of about $600,150.75, the $550,150.75 commitment to the Grizzly Flats program, forgivable loans up to $73,318, and that the fund has no specific restrictions. Balance after the commitment was $0 with funds continuing to accrue from permit activity, so nothing is currently available for multifamily. prevailing_wage_trigger is true with no cited basis; not reviewed in this audit.

reason: Fund deploys forgivable loans at Board discretion per Board item 26-0542, so funding_type is loan rather than other.

set.typical_award_size: None. The County Developer Programs page lists only the Traffic Impact Fee (TIF) Offset and Collaborative Opportunities; no general affordable housing fee waiver or reimbursement program is offered to developers. The TIF offset (Policy B-14) is the only fee incentive. The separate Building Fee Deferral Program (listed under Homebuyers, page live on November 8, 2026) lets very low-income applicants defer building fees on new construction or health and safety repair permits until refinancing, resale or change in ownership; new guidelines are marked coming soon and it is aimed at individual homeowners, not multifamily developments. School, fire and other agency impact fees are not waived: Racquet Way Phase 2 (24 units) still owed about $87,360 to the Office of Education and $36,240 to the fire district after a 50% TIF offset was recommended.
set.layering_notes: Negative finding recorded so the fee line is budgeted in full. Use the full 2025 TIF schedule less the B-14 offset on income-restricted units, plus full school, fire and County building and planning fees. The Building Fee Deferral Program is a homebuyer-side program for very low-income applicants; confirm with the Planning and Building Department (530-621-5824, Loans@edcgov.us) before assuming it covers a multifamily project.
set.audit_note: Reclassified fee waiver to negative finding because no waiver program exists. Building Fee Deferral page was reachable via WebFetch on November 8, 2026 (curl returns 403 Access Denied).

reason: Developer Programs page confirms no waiver beyond the TIF offset, and the Building Fee Deferral page is live with homebuyer-only terms, so award text and funding_type were corrected.

set.audit_note: Confirmed against the August 2026 public review draft Housing Element (pages 4-176 to 4-178, 4-203 to 4-206 and the Program 1-7 review): Council waiver for nonprofits and public agencies under Section 6.55.090 with about 45 days to approval, Sugar Pine Village inspection fee reduction, Program 1-7 fee waiver for designated affordable units in lot consolidations, TRPA $1.86 per sq ft water quality and $8.50 per sq ft excess coverage fees with no affordable exemption, mobility fee waivable, STPUD $7,500 deposit and 10% capacity fee down payment. Section 6.55.090 itself was not read. prevailing_wage_trigger is true with no cited basis; the Housing Element prevailing wage section is general and does not address fee waivers.

reason: Housing Element draft supports award, eligibility, cycle and fee figures, so confidence was raised to verified with no fact changes.
